records.statement: Class shape: MemrefAliasAnalysisState wraps a single private llvm::EquivalenceClasses<Value> aliasInfo (with an LLVM-22-compatible variant selected by __LLVM_MAJOR_VERSION_22_COMPATIBLE__); public API is constructor(Operation*), unionAliasSets(v1,v2), createAliasInfoEntry(v), printAlias(), isAlias(v1,v2); the header comment states 'Alias analysis of memref, greatly borrowed from OneShotAnalysisState'.

Seeding: the constructor walks the given op and calls createAliasInfoEntry — aliasInfo.insert(v) — for every memref-typed op result and every memref-typed block argument in all regions; non-memref values are never inserted.
Union: unionAliasSets returns silently unless BOTH values are MemRefType, else aliasInfo.unionSets(v1, v2); isAlias is aliasInfo.isEquivalent(v1, v2); createAliasInfoEntry is aliasInfo.insert(v).

Consumer: MergeVecScopePass is the only user outside the class's own files — it constructs the state over the root (MergeVecScope.cpp:529), unions every alias pair from hivm::getOperationAliasInfo (MergeVecScope.cpp:534-542), passes state.isAlias as the predicate into analyzeMemrefDepdencies (MergeVecScope.cpp:562), and calls state.printAlias() unconditionally (MergeVecScope.cpp:544).

Alias-pair sources: getOperationAliasInfo (Utils.cpp:1158-1200+) returns pairs for arith::SelectOp (result↔true/false), bufferization ToMemref/ToBuffer/ToTensor (result↔operand), hivm::BitcastOp, memref::CastOp/CollapseShapeOp/ExpandShapeOp/ExtractStridedMetadataOp/MemorySpaceCastOp/ReinterpretCastOp/ReshapeOp, and more — i.e. view/cast/select style ops whose result aliases an existing value.

Executed build/bin/bishengir-opt --debug-only=hivm-utils --hfusion-merge-vf=merge-level=2 on bishengir/test/Dialect/HIVM/RegBase/merge-vf-level-2.mlir (exit 0): printAlias dumped the equivalence classes — allocs and VF call results appear as singleton sets, while subview results are merged with their view sources: {%subview of %arg0, block-arg memref<256x128xf32> index 0}, {%subview_7, %subview_6, block-arg memref<256xf32> index 2}, {%subview_9, %subview_5, block-arg memref<256x128xf32> index 1} — unions fired through view-source alias pairs.

Executed the same binary with --debug-only=hivm-utils on the tensor-form merge-vf-level-1.mlir (exit 0): the dump shows exactly one alias set with one member (a block argument of type memref<16x128xf16>) — a tensor-form root yields almost no memref values, so the state is nearly empty; no unions fired.

History: the class arrived with the A5 migration commit 4ddead06f (2026-07-15, same commit that introduced MergeVecScope) and was adapted for LLVM 22 in 47f2a3254 (2026-07-22, 'fix: fix llvm-22') — matching the two compile-time variants in the header/print code.
No dedicated unit test: the class has no test file of its own under bishengir/test; it is exercised only through consumers (the merge-vf-* lit fixtures cover it indirectly via MergeVecScope).

Why union-find here: the consumer needs a transitive 'may-alias' relation — after subview A aliases its source B, and B aliases another view C, all three must query equal; llvm::EquivalenceClasses gives exactly that with near-linear amortized unions. Inferred from the query pattern (isAlias used pairwise inside an O(n²) dependency scan) — no comment states the complexity rationale.

The memref-only type guard makes the class total over the module: seeding inserts only memref values and unionAliasSets refuses mixed-type pairs, so non-memref values can never join a class — this keeps isAlias answers closed over the seeded domain. Inferred from the guard placement (EV-102/EV-103).
